content.text:
I submitted index 7 (Ni 0.29, V 0.71), which gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured: 1.14e-6 A. The episode is closed.

| Index | Ni fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.65 | 7e-8 |
| 0 | 0.34 | 4.8e-7 |
| 7 | 0.29 | 1.14e-6 |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose steadily as the vanadium fraction went up. The last point was still the highest, so the best composition in the library may lie further toward vanadium than anything I measured.
- **Why I chose these points:** the stability model (MACE) found NiV2O6, at Ni 0.33, to be the most stable nickel–vanadium phase. The band-gap model (MEGNet) put its gap at about 2.5 eV, below the 3.22 eV light, so it can absorb. Index 0 sits at that composition, so I measured it first. Index 14 tested the nickel-rich side, and index 7 took a moderate step toward vanadium.
- **Main open question:** I didn't measure the vanadium-rich end (indices 3, 8, 11, 13). The Gaussian-process tool suggested index 8, but I went with index 7 as the smaller step. Both models were unfavourable toward the one vanadium-rich compound listed, Ni2V8O15: it came out well above the stability line, with a predicted gap of only 0.9 eV. So I expected that end to split into NiV2O6 plus V2O5 rather than form a better absorber.
- **Unused budget:** I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases are actually present was never checked.
